description: EoE review consult using detailed mode. Complex consultation — multiple active problems, treatment response, dietary restrictions, ongoing dose titration. Tests: detailed mode completeness, multiple active problem handling, dose titration, EoE routing (REVIEW_LETTER not FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW_LETTER).
transcript:
Gastroenterologist: Good afternoon Benjamin. Last time I saw you was about eight months ago. You've had eosinophilic oesophagitis confirmed on biopsy — eosinophil count was 25 per high-power field — and you've been on swallowed fluticasone 500 micrograms twice daily since then. How has the dysphagia been?

Patient: It's improved quite a lot actually. I used to get food stuck every week. Now it's maybe once every three to four weeks. Still happening but less.

Gastroenterologist: Good, that's a partial response. He also has an associated atopic background — asthma and allergic rhinitis — and he's on a dairy and wheat free diet under the guidance of his dietitian Sarah Chen. He's maintained his weight. Let me look at his recent bloods — eosinophil count on blood is borderline elevated at 0.6 times ten to the nine per litre. I want to repeat the endoscopy with biopsies to formally assess mucosal response.

Patient: Will I need a higher dose?

Gastroenterologist: Possibly. If the repeat biopsy still shows greater than 15 eosinophils per high-power field despite the fluticasone, I'll consider increasing the dose to 500 micrograms three times daily, or discussing a proton pump inhibitor trial to see if there's a PPI-responsive component. He also mentioned some reflux symptoms have emerged over the past two months — mild, post-prandial — which may represent a PPI-responsive EoE subtype or co-existing GORD.

Patient: I'm worried about long-term steroid use.

Gastroenterologist: That's a reasonable concern. Swallowed topical steroids at this dose have a low systemic absorption profile, but it's worth discussing. I have arranged a repeat OGD for next month. Depending on those biopsy results I will review his management. No immediate GP action required at this stage. I'll continue to manage his EoE in my clinic.
